title: Payments, Late Fees and Returned Payments on PracticePay Patient Financing
content:
**Accepting payments.** Payments on a PracticePay Patient Financing plan are accepted on a plan in active or charged-off status, as the plan's record shows.

**Applying payments.**

- *Allocation clause (no longer in force).* The clause that each payment is applied to billed interest and billed deferred interest first, then fees, then the remaining plan balance is no longer in force as written; it is superseded by the current terms for a payment reset of a PracticePay plan.
- A monthly payment counts as made once payments credited toward it reach the monthly payment amount, and amounts beyond the payments due reduce the balance without advancing the next due date.
- Payments submitted by the same-day cutoff Eastern Time on a business day are effective that day; a debit card payment may not exceed the plan's largest single debit card payment.

**When a late fee may be assessed.** A late fee may be assessed only when the current date is later than the monthly due date plus the late-fee grace period. The grace period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the monthly due date.

| Day (counting from the day after the monthly due date) | Late fee may be assessed |
|---|---|
| the last day of the grace period (the 10th day on a 10-day grace period) | no |
| the day after it (the 11th day) | yes |

**Amount of the late fee — clause no longer in force.** The clause that the late fee is the plan's flat late fee but never more than the unpaid part of that monthly payment, at most the plan's number of late fees per due date, with the amount of an open billing dispute left out of the unpaid part, is no longer in force as written; it is superseded by the current late-fee schedule of PracticePay Patient Financing.

**Provider refunds.** A provider refund never counts as a payment toward a monthly payment due.

**Returned payments.** A returned payment is reversed in full and the monthly payment it covered is unpaid again.

**Returned-payment fee — clause no longer in force.** The clause that a returned-payment fee of the plan's flat returned-payment fee is charged once per returned payment whose return code is one of the fee-bearing return codes, never for R07, R10, R29 or a chargeback, is no longer in force as written; it is superseded by the current returned-payment fee schedule of PracticePay Patient Financing.

**Records.** Balances and delinquency fields are refreshed after every line.

superseded_clauses: The late fee is late_fee_usd but never more than the unpaid part of that monthly payment, at most max_late_fees_per_due_date per due date, and the amount of an open billing dispute is left out of the unpaid part.
a returned-payment fee of returned_payment_fee_usd is charged once per returned payment whose return code is in fee_bearing_return_codes, never for R07, R10, R29 or a chargeback
